Remember this: Chemistry Teachers, Postsecondary oversee how knowledge is passed on, while research determines how knowledge grows. One emphasizes teaching and the other discovery, and colleges often bind the two together.

A poor fit for people who dislike lesson preparation, cannot sit with the literature, or cannot tolerate student questions. Much of the work moves among the classroom, laboratory, and research papers.

A common path is: doctorate in chemistry or a related field -> postdoctoral work -> college teaching assistant or lecturer -> independent teaching and lab supervision -> promotion to associate professor -> professor or disciplinary leadership.

A good fit for people who investigate deeply, communicate clearly, pay attention to detail, and insist that students truly understand. If making ideas clear is your baseline, this career can be stable.
